chapter_title_ka: წასლვა ავთანდილისაგან ნესტან დარეჯანის საძებრად და ქარავანთა შეყრა
chapter_title_en: Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ყმა მიმავალი მიუბნობს, მსგავსი მთვარისა სრულისა.
არს თინათინის გონება მისად სალხენად გულისა;
იტყვის: “მოგშორდი, — სიცრუვე, ვა, საწუთროსა კრულისა! —
და შენ გაქვს წამალი ჩემისა მამრთელებელი წყლულისა.
stanzas.english_translation: The knight speaks as he goes on his way (majestically) like the full moon; there is the thought of T’hinat’hin to gladden his heart. He says: "I am far from thee; alas! the falseness of cursed Fate! Thou hast the healing balsam for my wound.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1025; Wardrop Stanza 1004): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რად სიცხე გულსა ნიადაგ მწვავს გმირსა სამს ალებისა;
რად გული კლდისა ტინისა შემქმნია სამ სალებისა!
არ შეუძლია ლახვარსა დაჩენა სამსა ლებისა,
და შენ ხარ მიზეზი სოფლისა ასრე გასამსალებისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "Why doth the ardour of grief for the heroes continually burn me? why is my heart of rock and cliff become a hard rock? even three lances cannot show a bruise on me. Thou art the cause that this world is thus envenomed for me."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1026; Wardrop Stanza 1005): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ მარტო ზღვის პირსა მივა ოთხითა მონითა,
წამალსა ტარიელისსა ეძებს ყოვლითა ღონითა,
დღისით და ღამით მტირალი იღვრების ცრემლთა ფონითა,
და ჩალად უჩნს ყოვლი ქვეყანა, მისვე ჩალისა წონითა.
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil fares on alone to the seashore with the four slaves, with all his might he seeks balm for Tariel; weeping by day and night he pours forth pools of tears; all the world seems to him as straw, even as straw in weight.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1027; Wardrop Stanza 1006): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
სადაცა ნახნის, ეუბნის, მგზავრნი ზღვის პირსა რებულნი,
ჰკითხის მის მზისა ამბავი; დღენი ვლნა გაასებულნი.
ქედსა გარდადგეს, აქლემნი აუჩნდეს ლარ-კიდებულნი.
და მოქარავნენი ზღვის პირსა დაყრით დგეს დაყმუნებულნი.
stanzas.english_translation: Wherever he sees travellers walking by the shore he addresses them, he asks tidings of that sun (Nestan). He roamed a hundred days. He went up a hill; camels loaded with stuff appeared; merchants distressed stood in perplexity on the shore.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1028; Wardrop Stanza 1007): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მუნ ქარავანი ურიცხვი იდგა მის ზღვისა კიდესა.
შეიჭირვებდეს, ჭმუნვიდეს, ვერცა დგეს, ვერცა ვლიდესა.
ყმამან სალამი უბრძანა, — ქებასა შეასხმიდესა,
და ჰკითხა თუ: “ვინ ხართ, ვაჭარნო?” – მათ საუბარი ჰკიდესა.
stanzas.english_translation: A countless caravan was there on the seashore, they were distressed, they were gloomy, they could neither stand nor go forward. The knight greeted them; they hailed him with praise. He asked: "Merchants, who are ye?" They began to converse.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1029; Wardrop Stanza 1008): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
უსამ იყო ქარავნისა უხუცესი, კაცი ბრძენი.
მოახსენა ხოტბა სრული, დალოცა და უქნა ზნენი.
ჰკადრეს: “ხმელთა სინათლეო, შენ ამოხვე ჩვენი მლხენი,
და ჩამოჰხე და მოგახსენოთ ამბავი და საქმე ჩვენი”.
stanzas.english_translation: Usam was the chief of the caravan, a wise man. He uttered respectfully a perfect eulogy, he invoked blessings on (Avt’handil) and praised his manners; he said: "O sun, thou art come as our life and comforter. Dismount; we will tell thee our story and business!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1030; Wardrop Stanza 1009): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
გარდაჰხდა. ჰკადრეს: “ჩვენ ვართო მობაღდადენი ვაჭარნი,
მაჰმადის სჯულის მჭირავნი, აროდეს გვისვამს მაჭარნი,
ზღვათა მეფისა ქალაქსა სავაჭროდ გარდმონაჭარნი,
და საქონელ-სრულნი, მდიდარნი, არ ლარნი გვაქვან ნაჭარნი.
stanzas.english_translation: He dismounted. They said: "We are Bagdad merchants, holders of the faith of Mahmad; we never drink new wines; we haste to trade in the city of the Sea-King; we are rich in wholesale goods, we have no cut pieces of stuff.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1031; Wardrop Stanza 1010): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: "Here on the seashore we found a man lying senseless; we succoured him till he could speak clearly with his tongue. We asked him: 'Who art thou, stranger? What business dost thou follow after?' He said to us: If ye go in they will slay you. It is well that I still live!'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1032; Wardrop Stanza 1011): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თქვა: “ქარავანი ეგვიპტით გამოვემართეთ ერითა,
ზღვასა შევედით ტვირთულნი ლარითა მრავალ-ფერითა,
მუნ მეკობრეთა დაგვხოცეს ძელის სახნისის წვერითა,
და ყველაი წახდა, არ ვიცი, აქა მოსრულვარ მე რითა!”
stanzas.english_translation: "He said: 'From Egypt we set out with a caravan and a guard, we embarked upon the sea laden with many kinds of stuff, there pirates (in ships) with sharp (iron) pointed wooden rams slew us. All was lost; I know not how I came hither.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1033; Wardrop Stanza 1012): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ლომო და მზეო, ესეა მიზეზი აქა დგომისა,
დაბრუნვებითა გვეცემის ზიანი არ-საზომისა;
შევიდეთ, ვა თუ დაგვხოცნენ, ძალი არა გვაქვს ომისა,
და ვერცა ვდგათ, ვერცა წასრულვართ, ღონე წაგვსლვია რჩომისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "O lion and sun, this is the reason of our standing here. If we return, our loss will be a hundredfold; if we embark, alas! they may slay us, we have no strength for battle. We cannot stay, we cannot go, the power to maintain ourselves is gone from us."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1034; Wardrop Stanza 1013): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: The knight said: "Whoever grieves is nought, and strives in vain; whatever comes from above, we cannot avoid its coming. I am surety for your blood, I take upon myself what you shall shed; whoever fights with you, my sword will wear itself out on your foes."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1035; Wardrop Stanza 1014): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: They of the caravan were filled with great joy; they said: "He is some knight, some hero, not timid like us, he has self-confidence, let us be calm in heart." They embarked, they went on board ship, they set out from the coast.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1036; Wardrop Stanza 1015): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
სიამოვნისა დარითა იარეს, არ სიძნელითა.
მათი ბადრაგა ავთანდილ უძღვის გულითა ქველითა.
გამოჩნდა ნავი მეკობრე დროშითა მეტად გრძელითა,
და მას ნავსა ნავთა სალეწლად სახნისი ჰგია ძელითა.
stanzas.english_translation: With pleasant weather they journeyed without hardship; their convoyer, Avt’handil, leads them with brave heart. A pirate ship appeared with an exceedingly long flag; that ship had an (iron-shod) plough with (beam of) wood for shattering ships.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1037; Wardrop Stanza 1016): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: (The pirates) yelled and came on, they shouted and trumpeted; the caravan was afraid of the multitude of those warriors. The knight spoke: "Fear not their hardihood; either I slay them all or this is the day of my death.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1038; Wardrop Stanza 1017): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: "Nought undecreed can they do to me, even if all the hosts on earth engage me: if it be decreed, I shall not survive, the spears are ready for me, neither strongholds nor friends, not even brothers, can save me; he who knows this is stout-hearted like me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1039; Wardrop Stanza 1018): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თქვენ, ვაჭარნი, ჯაბანნი ხართ, ომისაცა უმეცარნი,
შორს ისრითა არ დაგხოცნენ, ჩაიხშენით თანა კარნი;
მარტო მნახეთ, ვით შევება, ვით ვიხმარნე ლომნი მკლავნი,
და მეკობრისა ნავისანი, სისხლნი ჰნახნეთ მონაღვარნი”.
stanzas.english_translation: "You merchants are cowards, unskilled in war. Lest they slay you with the arrow from afar, shut the doors behind you. Behold me alone how I fight, how I use my lion-like arms; see how I make the blood of the corsair's crew flow."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1040; Wardrop Stanza 1019): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ჩაიცვა ტანსა აბჯარი ქცევითა ვეფხებრ მკრჩხალითა.
მას ხელთა კეტი რკინისა ჰქონდა ხელითა ცალითა;
ნავისა თავსა გულითა წადგა შიშ-შეუვალითა,
და ვითა მჭვრეტელნი ჭვრეტითა, მტერნი დახოცნა ხრმალითა.
stanzas.english_translation: With gesture like a swift panther he clad his form in armour; in one hand he held an iron mace. He stood forth with dauntless heart in the front of the ship, and as he slew onlookers with his gaze, so he slew foes with his sword.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1041; Wardrop Stanza 1020): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
კიოდეს იგი ლაშქარნი, ხმა მათი არ გაწყდებოდა,
აძგერეს ძელი, რომელსა ზედა სახნისი ჰგებოდა;
ყმა ნავის თავსა უშიშრად ქვე დგა, არ თურე კრთებოდა,
და კეტი ჰკრა, ძელი მოსტეხა; ლომს მკლავი არ უდრკებოდა.
stanzas.english_translation: (a)The beam was destroyed, and Avt’handil remained with ship unshattered. Those warriors feared, they sought a way to shelter, they could not contrive it in time; he leaped on his foes, threshing them down round about him; there was not left there living man unhacked by him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1042; Wardrop Stanza 1021): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: With intrepid heart he slew those warriors like goats; some he threw down on the ship, some he cast into the sea; he threw one upon another, eight upon nine and nine upon eight; those who were left were hidden among the corpses, they stifled their cries.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1043; Wardrop Stanza 1022): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.english_translation: As much as his heart desired was he victorious in the fight with them. Some humbly adjured him: "Slay us not, by thy faith!" Those he slew not, he enslaved them, whoever survived his wounds. Truly saith the Apostle: "Fear makes love."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 42 ('Departure of Avtandil to Seek Nestan-Darejan and Meeting the Caravan', Stanza 1044; Wardrop Stanza 1023): Part of the narrative sequence in which applying analytical deduction (as highlighted by Academician Elguja Khintibidze), Avtandil travels to the sea crossroads where all ships harbor, meets the terrified merchant caravan of Usen, single-handedly boards and destroys a pirate corsair ship, and assumes the disguise of merchant chief 'Abdal-Mesi' to investigate Gulansharo without arousing suspicion.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
გაუმარჯვდა ომი მათი, ვითა სწადდა მისა გულსა.
ზოგთა ჰკადრეს ზენაარი: “ნუ დაგვხოცო, შენსა სჯულსა!”
არ დახოცნა, დაიმონნა, დარჩომოდა რაცა წყლულსა.
და მართლად იტყვის მოციქული — “შიში შეიქმს სიყვარულსა”.
stanzas.english_translation: O man! boast not of thy strength, brag not drunken like! Might is of none avail if the power of the Lord aid thee not. A tiny spark overcomes, and burns up great trees. If God protect thee, it cuts alike well whether thou strike with a log or a sword.

stanzas.english_translation: There Avt’handil saw their great treasures. He grappled twin-like ship to ship. He called the caravan. Usam was merry when he saw, he rejoiced, he lamented not, he spoke a eulogy in his praise, he gave form to great imaginings.

stanzas.english_translation: Praisers of Avt’handil need even a thousand tongues; even they could not tell how fair he appeared after the fight. The caravan shouted, saying: "Lord, thanks to Thee! The sun has shed down on us his beams; the dark night has broken into day for us."

stanzas.english_translation: They came up to him, they kissed his head, face, feet, hand; they spoke praise unstinted to the fair, the praiseworthy; the sight of him maddens the wise man as well as the fool!" We all are saved by thee in so hard a mischance."

stanzas.english_translation: "God hath deigned to spare your blood, so many souls! I, alas! vain earth, what am I? Of myself, what have I done? Now I have slain your foes, I have fulfilled what I spoke; I have brought you the ship complete with its wealth as a gift."

stanzas.english_translation: Pleasant it is when a good knight has won the battle, when he has surpassed his comrades who were with him. They congratulated him, they praised him, in this state they were ashamed. The wound becomes him well, but little was he hurt.

stanzas.english_translation: That day they looked at that ship of the corsairs, they put not off till the morrow. How could they count the quantity of treasure lying there! They conveyed it to their ship, they completely emptied the (pirate) ship; they smashed it up and burned some of it; the wood they bartered not for sixpence.

stanzas.english_translation: "As much treasure as I desired to amass I had of mine own, countless priceless coverlets of silk. What use could I make of yours? What do I want? I am but your companion. Moreover, I have some other dangerous business.

stanzas.english_translation: "Now, of this countless treasure I have found here, take what you each wish; I shall be a claimant against none. One thing I entreat: grant my request, one not to be mistrusted; I have a certain matter to be kept hidden within you.

stanzas.english_translation: "Till the time comes, speak not of me as if I were not your master. Say, 'He is our chief,' call me not knight. I will clothe myself as a merchant, I will begin chaffering; keep the secret, by the brotherhood between us."

stanzas.english_translation: This thing very greatly rejoiced the caravan; they came and saluted him, saying: "It is our hope--the very request we should have made to you, you yourself have made to us--that we may serve him whose face we acknowledge as the face of the sun."

stanzas.english_translation: Thence they departed and travelled on, they wasted no time; they met fair weather, they sailed ever pleasantly; they delighted in Avt’handil, they sang his praises; they presented him with a pearl of the tint of the knight's teeth.
